results.summary:
Track complete: all 4 child nodes landed and merged to main, and the root's own integration pass is draft PR #60 on branch kb/51 (based on main).

WHAT EACH NODE LANDED
#52 (PR #56, merged) — LICENSE (MIT; the license field had been claiming MIT with no file behind it), author/homepage/bugs, keywords, and publishConfig {access: public, provenance: true}. Audited `files` against every runtime read: it needed no change. No .npmignore, deliberately. KEY FACT: the npm name `hkb` is unclaimed (npm view hkb → E404).
#54 (PR #57, merged) — README now opens on the adopter: `npx hkb init` quickstart, badges, a ten-line "how it works", then the philosophy bullets. The self-hosting narrative and the four `hkb doctor --api` observations moved to the new docs/status.md, with the reason each is load-bearing and an honest "what is not proven yet".
#53 (PR #58, merged) — .github/workflows/release.yml: a `v*` tag runs the suite, refuses a tag that disagrees with package.json (naming both numbers and the fix), preflights NPM_TOKEN into a ::notice:: rather than a red build, publishes with --provenance, then a second job with NO checkout runs `npx -y hkb@<version> version` and `help` against the registry copy, retrying 10× 30s for propagation. Plus docs/releasing.md and 20 tests that EXECUTE the gate and the retry loop under a stubbed PATH rather than regexing them.
#55 (PR #59, merged) — scripts/smoke-pack.mjs: pack → install the tarball into an empty dir → run the CLI from where npm put it (version must match the installed package.json, help must be the help, `hook stop` with no KB_TASK must exit 0), plus 16 must-ship files each annotated with the line that reads it and 7 must-NOT-ship paths (without which deleting `files` outright would ship the whole repo and every other check would still pass). Wired as a `smoke` job in test.yml on Node 20 — the floor `engines` claims and nothing else checked.

THE ROOT'S OWN PASS (PR #60) — the seam no child could see, because each only had its own paths:
release.yml re-runs lint and the suite ITSELF rather than depending on the test.yml workflow, so #55's smoke job gated pushes and PRs but never a release — the one place a bad tarball does real damage. Both nodes were correct inside their scope; the gap only existed between them. Fixed: release.yml now runs `npm run smoke` before the publish step, and test/release.test.js asserts the ordering and that test.yml still carries the job it mirrors. Also: `npm run smoke` is now a script rather than a path repeated in two workflows; `lint` covers scripts/*.mjs (smoke-pack.mjs was the one file in the repo nothing checked); the README's Docs section links docs/releasing.md (#53 wrote the page, #54 built the section, neither could touch the other's file); docs/status.md gains the tarball to its verified list and drops a test count that #53 had already made stale; CLAUDE.md tells the next contributor when to run the smoke.

VERIFIED OVER THE WHOLE RESULT: npm run lint clean (and now actually covering scripts/); npm test 412 pass / 0 fail; all four workflows parse under test/yaml.js and all 18 of their `run:` blocks syntax-check under bash -n; every relative link in README.md, docs/status.md, docs/releasing.md and docs/harnesses.md resolves, anchors included; npm pack --dry-run is 41 files / 150.3 kB with scripts/ correctly not shipped; smoke-pack re-run against a package tree built from the updated files[] passes 23 content + 3 command checks, and fails with 4 named fixes when skills/ is dropped.

STILL OPEN, and exactly what the track put out of scope: the operator creates the token (`npm token create --read-only=false && gh secret set NPM_TOKEN`) and pushes the tag (`npm version 0.1.0 --allow-same-version && git push --follow-tags`). Until NPM_TOKEN exists a tag runs the whole workflow, prints a ::notice:: with that first command, and publishes nothing. PR #60 is the last piece to merge; check the `packed artifact` job is green on main before tagging.
